title: Imports and Setup
content:
We import Mathlib's group theory foundations: **cosets**, **subgroup index**, **rational arithmetic**, and **finite type cardinality**.

These provide the building blocks for defining exact coverings of groups by cosets.
mathContext: The key import is `Subgroup.index` which gives [G:H], the index of H in G.

title: Exact Covering Structure
content:
An **exact covering** of a group G by k cosets consists of:
- k subgroups H₁, ..., Hₖ
- k coset representatives g₁, ..., gₖ
- A partition property: every element of G belongs to exactly one coset gᵢHᵢ

This formalizes the notion of partitioning G by cosets.
mathContext: The cosets gᵢHᵢ = {gᵢh : h ∈ Hᵢ} are the left cosets. The covers field uses ∃! for exactly-one membership.

title: Distinct Indices Property
content:
A covering has **distinct indices** if all the subgroup indices [G:Hᵢ] are pairwise different.

The Herzog-Schönheim conjecture asks: can such a covering exist with k > 1?
mathContext: The index [G:H] counts how many cosets of H partition G. If G is finite, [G:H] = |G|/|H|.

title: Herzog-Schönheim Conjecture
content:
The **Herzog-Schönheim Conjecture** states that no group G can be exactly covered by k > 1 cosets with all distinct indices.

Equivalently: if cosets partition G, at least two must have the same index.
mathContext: This is a deep statement about the structure of subgroups. It connects to Egyptian fractions since the indices must satisfy 1/n₁ + ... + 1/nₖ = 1.

title: Sun's Theorem (Axiom)
content:
**Sun Zhi-Wei (2004)** proved the Herzog-Schönheim conjecture for finite abelian groups.

This is stated as an axiom because the proof requires deep results about the structure of abelian groups not formalized in Mathlib.
mathContext: Sun's proof actually shows more: it works for any collection of subnormal subgroups, which includes all subgroups when G is abelian.

title: Equivalent Formulation
content:
An equivalent statement: for any exact covering of a finite abelian group with k > 1 cosets, there exist distinct i, j with [G:Hᵢ] = [G:Hⱼ].

This is derived from Sun's axiom by negating the distinct indices condition.
mathContext: The `push_neg` tactic transforms ¬(∀i j, i≠j → n_i≠n_j) into ∃i j, i≠j ∧ n_i=n_j.

title: Computational Verification
content:
**Margolis and Schnabel (2019)** verified computationally that the conjecture holds for all groups of order < 1440.

This is the best known computational result, extending the verified cases significantly.
mathContext: The bound 1440 comes from systematic enumeration. The smallest potential counterexample would need |G| ≥ 1440.

title: Main Result: Abelian Case Solved
content:
We prove that the Herzog-Schönheim conjecture holds for finite abelian groups using Sun's axiom.

This answers Erdős Problem #274 for the abelian case: NO, you cannot partition an abelian group by cosets with distinct indices.
mathContext: The proof is a direct application of sun_abelian_case.

title: Index Sum Condition
content:
A **necessary condition** for k cosets to partition G: the reciprocals of indices must sum to 1.

If cosets have indices n₁, ..., nₖ, then 1/n₁ + ... + 1/nₖ = 1.

**Example:** Indices 2, 3, 6 satisfy 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 1.
mathContext: This follows from counting: |G| = Σ|Hᵢ| = Σ(|G|/nᵢ), so 1 = Σ(1/nᵢ). Axiomatized as the sum ∑ 1/[G:Hᵢ] = 1 over ℚ.

title: Summary
content: erdos_274_summary: The abelian case of the Herzog-Schönheim conjecture is proved via Sun's theorem. The general case remains OPEN.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of summary
